title: Small words that matter, and the A1 check (Kleine Wörter)
summary: The last A1 words: wissen and kennen, warum, bald, gleich, kaputt, möglich and more. Then check your A1: the final test and the Goethe A1 mock exam.
goals: Use everyday little words: warum, bald, gleich, sofort, mehr, nichts
Check your level: the A1 final test and the mock exam

points: A 20-question multiple-choice quiz on the whole of A1. Answer before the video shows the solution (15 seconds each).

It checks verb endings ([[Ich heiße Lena.]]), du or Sie ([[Wie geht's? - Gut, und dir?]]), articles ([[Die Tasche kostet zwanzig Euro.]]), opposites ([[Die Lampe ist teuer.]], the opposite of [[billig]]), and [[ein]] or [[eine]] ([[Das ist eine Couch.]]).
Word order: separable verbs ([[Ich kaufe heute ein.]]), modal verbs ([[Max kann gut Englisch.]]), [[um]] with clock times.
Cases: [[mir]], not mich, with [[gefallen]] ([[Das gefällt mir.]]); [[mit]] + dative ([[mit dem Fahrrad]]); the accusative ([[Wie findest du diesen Pullover?]]).
Also: [[man]] takes the er/sie/es form, the Perfekt of [[gehen]] takes [[sein]] ([[Ich bin gegangen.]]), and a polite reply at the shop ([[Ich hätte gern ein Kilo Birnen.]]).

phrases.en: Hello, my name is Lena.
How are you? Fine, and you?
The bag costs twenty euros.

phrases.de: Ich hätte gern ein Kilo Birnen.
phrases.en: I'd like a kilo of pears.
Max speaks good English.
I like that.
I'm going by bike.
I went home.
What do you think of this jumper?

points: Time adverbs answer three questions: [[wann?]] (when), [[wie lange?]] (how long) and [[wie oft?]] (how often). They can start a sentence; the verb stays second: [[Manchmal habe ich Kopfschmerzen.]]
Regular times with -s: [[montags]], [[sonntags]], [[morgens]], [[mittags]], [[abends]], [[nachts]]: [[Er arbeitet gern sonntags.]]

Past: [[vorgestern]], [[gestern]], [[früher]] (in the past), [[damals]] (back then). Now: [[heute]], [[jetzt]], [[gerade]] (right now), [[sofort]] (at once), [[heutzutage]] (nowadays). Future: [[morgen]], [[übermorgen]], [[bald]], [[später]].
Careful: [[morgen]] is tomorrow; [[morgens]] is in the morning.
Order of events: [[vorher]] (before), [[zuerst]], [[dann]], [[danach]], [[später]].
How often, from most to least: [[immer]], [[meistens]], [[oft]] or [[häufig]], [[manchmal]] or [[ab und zu]], [[selten]], [[fast nie]], [[nie]].

phrases.en: In the evenings we all go for a walk.

phrases.de: Früher habe ich kein Gemüse gegessen.
phrases.en: I didn't use to eat vegetables.

phrases.de: Damals war ich ein kleiner Junge.
phrases.en: Back then I was a little boy.
She's on the phone right now.
She's having a baby soon.
Shall I call you later?

phrases.de: Danach gehen wir einkaufen, und später essen wir Eis.
phrases.en: After that we'll go shopping, and later we'll have ice cream.
He's always late.

phrases.de: Ich liebe meine Arbeit, aber ab und zu brauche ich eine Pause.
phrases.en: I love my work, but now and then I need a break.
I've never seen him.

points: [[warum]] (why) asks for a reason. It stands first, with the verb second: [[Warum lernst du Deutsch?]]
The answer usually comes with [[weil]] or [[denn]] (because), both at A2. For now, answer with a separate sentence.
Words with the same meaning, used the same way: [[wieso]], [[weshalb]], [[weswegen]]: [[Wieso ist er nicht gekommen?]]

phrases.en: Why are you learning German?
Why didn't he come?
Why don't you have time?

phrases.de: Weshalb kommst du heute so spät?
phrases.en: Why are you so late today?

phrases.de: Warum kommst du nicht? Ich bin krank.
phrases.en: Why aren't you coming? I'm ill.

notes.extra: [[wieso]], [[weshalb]] and [[weswegen]], which mean the same as [[warum]].

points: [[sehr]] is about quality: 'very' before an adjective: [[Du siehst heute sehr schön aus.]], [[Meine Kollegin ist sehr sympathisch.]]
[[sehr]] after a verb means 'very much', how strongly you feel: [[Die Pizza schmeckt ihm sehr.]], [[Diese Schuhe gefallen mir sehr.]]
[[viel]] is about quantity: 'much', 'a lot', after the verb: [[Das Handy kostet nicht viel.]], [[Er redet viel.]]
[[viel]] also goes before nouns you can't count: [[viel Zeit]], [[viel Geld]], [[viel Glück]].
They combine: [[sehr viel]] (a great deal), [[so viel]] (so much), [[zu viel]] (too much).

phrases.en: I like this film very much.
He really likes the pizza.
He didn't eat much.
Today I have a lot of time.

phrases.de: Auf der Party haben wir sehr viel gegessen.
phrases.en: We ate a great deal at the party.
He drinks so much coffee.
The music is very loud.
I wish you good luck.

points: Like much and many in English: [[viel]] with things you can't count (singular), [[viele]] with things you can count (plural).
[[viel]]: [[Ich habe nicht viel Zeit.]], [[Wie viel Geld hast du?]], [[Iss nicht so viel Fleisch!]]
[[viele]]: [[Sie hat viele Blusen gekauft.]], [[Wie viele Kinder hast du?]]
After a dative preposition, [[viele]] becomes [[vielen]]: [[Ich habe mit vielen Leuten Englisch gesprochen.]]

phrases.en: I don't have much time.
How much money do you have?
He has a lot of work today.
She bought lots of blouses.

phrases.de: Ich habe gestern viele Leute kennengelernt.
phrases.en: I met lots of people yesterday.
There are a lot of people here.

phrases.de: Ich habe mit vielen Leuten Englisch gesprochen.
phrases.en: I spoke English with lots of people.

points: Say them differently: [[wen]] has a long e, [[wenn]] a short e, [[wann]] an a. A wrong sound changes the meaning.
[[wen]] (whom) is the accusative of [[wer]] and always asks about a person: [[Wen rufst du an?]] - [[Ich rufe Peter an.]] Also after accusative prepositions: [[Für wen kaufst du ein Geschenk?]]
[[wann]] (when?) asks about a time: [[Wann kommen Sie?]] Answer with a time ([[um neun]], [[am Abend]]) or a time word ([[jeden Abend]], [[täglich]]).
[[wenn]] (if, whenever) is not a question word: it sets a condition and sends the verb to the end: [[Wenn ich Hunger habe, esse ich eine Banane.]] (A2)
In indirect questions (A2) the verb also goes last: [[Ich weiß nicht, wann er nach Hause kommt.]]

phrases.de: Wen rufst du an? Ich rufe Peter an.
phrases.en: Who are you calling? I'm calling Peter.

phrases.de: Für wen kaufst du ein Geschenk?
phrases.en: Who are you buying a present for?
When are you going to Berlin?
When does the class start?

phrases.de: Wenn ich Hunger habe, esse ich eine Banane.
phrases.en: When I'm hungry, I eat a banana.

phrases.de: Kannst du mir helfen, wenn ich etwas nicht verstehe?
phrases.en: Can you help me if I don't understand something?

phrases.de: Wenn ich krank bin, bleibe ich im Bett.
phrases.en: When I'm ill, I stay in bed.

phrases.de: Ich weiß nicht, wann er nach Hause kommt.
phrases.en: I don't know when he's coming home.

notes.extra: [[wenn]] (if, whenever), which sends the verb to the end; it comes properly at A2.

sections.title: wissen or kennen?
sections.text:
- [[wissen]] = to know a fact: [[Ich weiß es nicht.]] = I don't know. [[Weißt du das?]]
- [[kennen]] (Unit 4) = to know a person or a place: [[Ich kenne Eva.]] [[Ich kenne München.]]

[[wissen]] works like the modal verbs: [[ich weiß]] = [[er weiß]], with no -t.
Russian знать covers both. German splits them, and so does Armenian: գիտեմ is [[ich weiß]] (a fact), ճանաչում եմ is [[ich kenne]] (a person).

sections.title: Little words you'll use every day
rows: I'm not from around here either.
Die Wohnung ist ruhig. Der Koffer ist leicht.
The flat is quiet. The suitcase is light.

sections.text:
[[Warum?]] For now, answer with a separate sentence: [[Warum kommst du nicht? - Ich bin krank.]] A2 adds [[weil]] (because) in Unit 9.

[[Ich bin auch fremd hier.]] is the polite answer when someone asks you the way and you don't know it.

Places you'll need: [[das Geschäft]] (shop), [[die Bäckerei]], [[die Polizei]], [[die Schule]]: [[Die Kinder sind in der Schule.]]

sections.title: Your A1 check
sections.text:
You've reached the end of A1. Two ways to see where you stand:
1. **The A1 final check** (the test at the end of this lesson) mixes all units.
2. **The Goethe A1 mock exam** (Start Deutsch 1): listening, reading, writing and speaking, about 80 minutes. Ask Claude to start it on the PC: Claude opens the exam and the audio, and grades your writing and your speaking answers (typed in the chat).

It's a level check, not a goal. The point is to see what needs more practice before A2.

items.de: Kennst du Eva? - Ja, ich kenne sie.
items.en: Do you know Eva? - Yes, I know her.

items.de: Mein Fahrrad ist kaputt. Kann man das reparieren?
items.en: My bike is broken. Can it be fixed?
I'd like to meet your family.

items.de: Die Bäckerei ist am Sonntag nur bis Mittag geöffnet.
items.en: On Sunday the bakery is only open until noon.
I'm not from around here either.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I don't know.
items.explanation: wissen: ich weiß, with no ending.

items.question: Which sentence means 'Do you know Eva?'
items.explanation: A person: kennen. A fact: wissen.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: See you soon!
Fill in the gap: My phone is broken.

items.explanation: möglich = possible. Geht das? (Unit 3) works too.
